# DateAdd

Adds an amount of a unit of time to a date.

## Signature

```jyro
# fragment
DateAdd(date, amount, unit)
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `date` | string | The date to add to: a string in one of the forms `ParseDate` accepts. A string in no accepted form is a runtime error, as is any other type, null included. |
| `amount` | number | The number of units to add: a whole number from -2147483648 to 2147483647, negative to go back in time. A fractional number, a number outside that range, or a value that is not a number, null included, is a runtime error. |
| `unit` | string | The unit of amount, one of `"day"`, `"days"`, `"week"`, `"weeks"`, `"month"`, `"months"`, `"year"`, `"years"`, `"hour"`, `"hours"`, `"minute"`, `"minutes"`, `"second"` or `"seconds"`, matched with no regard to the case of ASCII letters. Any other string is a runtime error, as is a value that is not a string, null included. |

## Returns

String. The date that results, in UTC to the millisecond, in the form `yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.fffZ`. A result before `0001-01-01T00:00:00.000Z` or after `9999-12-31T23:59:59.999Z` is a runtime error. Never null.

## Remarks

Adding months or years keeps the day of the month where the new month has it, and otherwise gives the last day of that month: one month after 2024-01-31 is 2024-02-29. The time of day is kept for every unit but hours, minutes and seconds.

## Example

`DateAdd("2024-01-15", 10, "days")` returns `"2024-01-25T00:00:00.000Z"`.

`DateAdd("2024-01-15T12:00:00Z", -2, "hours")` returns `"2024-01-15T10:00:00.000Z"`.
